newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end down as bank warning sinks in.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end down as bank warning sinks in.

text.p: Late selling erased a sharply higher opening sent Taiwan shares to a lower close on Thursday as investors digested a central bank call for extra caution in the red-hot stock market, brokers said.
The index ended down 71.70 points or 0.83 percent at 8,584.12, well back from an opening high of 8,758.41.
Once again, turnover was huge at T$197 billion, though well below Tuesday's all-time record T$239 billion.
"Seeing the sharply higher opening, cautious investors stepped to the sidelines to await the central bank's next move," said HSBC James Capel senior analyst Alex Chen.

Central bank deputy governor Hsu Chia-tung warned after Wednesday's close that Taiwan's stock market turnover rate and price-earnings ratio were far higher than other countries' and urged caution now that a March correction had been overcome.
"Investors should be risk-conscious and be extra careful. What the central bank can do has already been done," Hsu said.
The central bank said it would issue T$3 billion in three-month negotiable certificates of deposit on Thursday.
The bank has consistently denied that its repeated issuance of the short-term instruments in recent weeks intended to take some of the fire from the sizzling stock market.
Analysts suspect otherwise, saying persistently loose liquidity has been a key factor driving a huge stock rally that has pushed the share index 25 percent higher in 1997 alone.

Brokers attributed the higher opening mainly to an early surge by financials as the Big Three state-run banks -- Chang Hwa, First and Hua Nan -- issued stock dividends of T$5, T$5 and T$2 per share, respectively.

Financials ended down 0.65 percent, but First Bank rose the seven percent limit to T$126.5 and Chang Hwa rose T$7 to T$125. Hua Nan rose T$3 to T$115 even though Moody's Investors Service had downgraded its financial strength rating to D+ from C.
